Base directory for this skill: checklist/indus-checklist/skills/advisor-checklist

# Advisor review checklist

1. Confirm which client and which accounts the task covers.
2. Use the most recent information available for the review date.
3. Check that positions and cash agree between statements and other records.
4. Check fees charged against the fee schedule.
5. Check the allocation against the investment policy statement.
6. Note anything unusual and say what follow-up it needs.
7. Say which records you relied on.

content.text:
No, not every 2025 RMD was met. The IRA requirement was more than covered, but the 401(k)'s own 2025 RMD of **$12,729.96** was never taken from the 401(k). Its deadline was 1 April 2026.

**Who owes and when.** Teodoro was born 14 March 1952, so he turned 73 in 2025. That makes 2025 his first RMD year, with a deadline of 1 April 2026. He owns all three retirement accounts and retired in 2019, so the still-working exception doesn't apply to the 401(k). Marguerite is 3.5 years younger, so the Uniform Lifetime Table applies, and its factor for age 73 is 26.5. Marguerite owns no retirement accounts here, so she owes nothing.

**What each account owed** (31 Dec 2024 balance ÷ 26.5):

| Account | 12/31/2024 balance | 2025 RMD |
|---|---|---|
| SYN-52710002 (IRA) | $623,678.60 | $23,535.04 |
| SYN-52710003 (rollover IRA) | $210,343.76 | $7,937.50 |
| SYN-52710004 (401(k)) | $337,343.96 | $12,729.96 |

**What was taken.** One distribution of $44,202.50 came from IRA ...002 on 4 December 2025, with $4,420.25 federal tax withheld. The transaction file and the 1099-R agree on this, and it matches the distribution form Teodoro signed on 24 November 2025.

- **IRAs:** Their RMDs can be added together and taken from either IRA. Together they owed $31,472.54, so the IRA requirement was covered.
- **401(k):** A 401(k)'s RMD has to come from the 401(k) itself. An IRA withdrawal doesn't count toward it. The $44,202.50 equals all three RMDs added together to the cent, so it looks like the 401(k)'s share was folded into the IRA withdrawal. No distribution appears in the 401(k)'s transactions through 15 April 2026 or on its Q1 2026 statement.

**Follow-up:**
- Take the missed $12,729.96 from the 401(k) now.
- Consider asking the IRS to waive the penalty on Form 5329, giving reasonable cause and showing it has been corrected. If it isn't waived, the penalty is normally 25% of the shortfall, or 10% if corrected promptly.
- The 2026 RMDs will also be due by 31 December 2026.
- The extra amount taken from the IRA can't be counted toward the 401(k) or toward 2026.
